summary: A small panel of content or controls, anchored to what opened it.

pairs.dont: Use a popover for a one-line explanation on hover.
pairs.do: Use Tooltip for explaining, Popover for content you interact with.
pairs.why: A popover takes focus and waits to be dismissed. That is too much ceremony for a sentence.

pairs.dont: Put a destructive confirmation in a popover.
pairs.do: Use Dialog when the answer matters and the page must wait.
pairs.why: A popover closes when you click away, so "are you sure?" can be dismissed by accident.

pairs.dont: Open a panel of controls with no title.
pairs.do: Add PopoverHeader with a title, or an aria-label on the content.
pairs.why: Radix does not name a popover for you the way it does a dialog. Without one a screen reader announces an unnamed group.

pairs.dont: Anchor to a container when a specific control opened it.
pairs.do: Let the trigger be the anchor, or use PopoverAnchor deliberately.
pairs.why: A panel that appears away from the thing you clicked reads as unrelated to it.

pairs.dont: Open a popover from inside a popover.
pairs.do: Put the second step in the same panel, or use a dialog.
pairs.why: Stacked dismiss-on-outside-click layers make Escape ambiguous and strand focus.

a11y: The panel points aria-labelledby and aria-describedby at its title and description, but only when those parts are actually present. A popover with neither is unnamed, which is correct for one that holds a single control.
Both ids come from useId, so two popovers on a page never collide.
Radix handles focus movement into the panel and back to the trigger on close; do not manage focus yourself.
